DEVELOPER DOCUMENTATION

How to Use CrossTalk

Get started in seconds with terminal commands, SDKs, or air-gapped single-file packages.

Terminal Single-Line Commands 
# 1. Join a channel across branches (auto-spawns hub if needed):
crosstalk up feature-auth --name "DevBot"

# 2. Generate a pairing invite with 3 options:
crosstalk invite --branch feature-auth --subnet 192.168.1.0/24

# 3. Join a friend's session from another branch:
crosstalk join XT-8A4F-AUTH --branch feature-ui

# 4. Check active agents and locked files:
crosstalk who
Zero Internet · Zero Dependencies · Single File

Copy a single file over USB or air-gapped LAN. Self-extracts and runs immediately.

Download crosstalk-airgap.sh (497 KB) Node Standalone (.mjs) Python Client (.py)
Run on Any Air-Gapped Machine 
# Run directly without installing:
sh crosstalk-airgap.sh who
sh crosstalk-airgap.sh up feature-auth
sh crosstalk-airgap.sh serve -s 192.168.1.0/24

# Or install permanently into PATH:
sh crosstalk-airgap.sh install
TypeScript / Node.js SDK 
import { CrossTalk } from 'cross-talk';

// Connect with branch context
const agent = await CrossTalk.join({ channel: 'feature-auth', name: 'Worker-1', branch: 'feature-auth' });

// Claim file lock before editing
agent.sendShorthand('!LCK @src/auth.ts #FEAT "oauth handler" &WAIT');

// Release lock upon completion
agent.sendShorthand('!REL @src/auth.ts &DONE &PROCEED');
Python SDK (Zero Third-Party Dependencies) 
from sdk.python.crosstalk import CrossTalkClient

client = CrossTalkClient(name="PyWorker", role="backend", url="ws://localhost:4488")
client.connect()

# Claim file using XDialect
client.send_shorthand('!LCK @app.py #FIX "crash bug" &WAIT')

# Release file lock when work finishes
client.send_shorthand('!REL @app.py &DONE &PROCEED')
Embedded C / Arduino Header (< 150 Bytes RAM) 
#include "crosstalk_micro.h"

void setup() {
    SerialBT.begin("CrossTalk-ESP32");
    // Send 34-byte lock claim over Bluetooth Serial or UART:
    CrossTalkMicro::claimLock(SerialBT, "src/sensor.h", XT_INTENT_FEAT, "IMU calibration", 60);
}

void loop() {
    // 100% static buffer - zero heap allocations!
}

ORIGINS & GITHUB REFERENCE

Inspired by PennyroyalTea/gibberlink

CrossTalk draws inspiration from Anton Pidkuiko & Boris Starkov’s viral Gibberlink (github.com/PennyroyalTea/gibberlink) at the ElevenLabs Hackathon. CrossTalk evolves this concept from acoustic audio modems into high-speed binary bitstreams, cooperative file locks, and zero-collision multi-agent coordination.
